messages.subject: Problem: Prediction of the response on a grid/map.
parts:
Hi.

I have binomial data (number of "successes" and "failures") for 1955 counties, and I would like to predict the missed 1154 counties and plot them on the US map.

pl.bound <- inla.sp2segment(sp)
coof <- as.matrix(df[, c("uscolong", "uscolat")])
mesh <- inla.mesh.create.helper(points = coof, boundary = pl.bound, cutoff = 0.7, max.edge = c(0.5, 5))    ### Can I make the mesh to have one point per county? Thnx. For spatial effect I need only county-neighbours.
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha = 2)
field.indices <- inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

proj_grid <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh, xlim = range(pl.bound$loc[, 1]), ylim = range(pl.bound$loc[, 2]), dims = nxy)

A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh, loc=coo)                                        ### coo - coords for available data
A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh, loc=coop)                                      ### coop - coords for unavailable data
stack.est <- inla.stack(data = list(y = df$r, numtrials = df$n),                     ### r - number of successes, n - total number of cases (successes + failures).
  A = list(A.est, 1), effects = list(c(field.indices, list(Intercept=1)),
    list(stco = df$stco)), tag="est")                                                ### stco - county code

stack.pred <- inla.stack(data = list(y = df$r, numtrials = df$n),                    ### df$r and df$n are NA
  A = list(A.pred, 1), effects = list(c(field.indices, list(Intercept=1)),
    list(stco = df$stco)), tag="pred")

stack <- inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred)
formula = y ~ -1 + Intercept + f(stco, model="iid", param=c(0.001,0.001)) + f(field, model=spde)

res <- inla(formula, data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde = spde), family = "binomial", Ntrials = numtrials, control.predictor= list(A = inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE, link=inla.stack.data(stack)$link))

I have a problem with extracting of the linear predictor values (or another summary) on the mesh.

xy.in <- inout(proj_grid$lattice$loc, pl.bound$loc)
g.mean2 <- inla.mesh.project(proj_grid, res$summary.linear.predictor$mean[pred.ind])
g.sd2 <- inla.mesh.project(proj_grid, res$summary.linear.predictor$sd[pred.ind])
g.mean2[!xy.in] <- g.sd2[!xy.in] <- NA

trellis.par.set(regions=list(col=terrain.colors(16)))
grid.arrange(levelplot(g.mean2, scales=list(draw=F), xlab='', ylab='', main='mean'),
levelplot(g.sd2, scal=list(draw=F), xla='', yla='', main='sd'), nrow = 2)             ### How can I add the borders of counties? Thnx.         




Summary vs Mesh:


























Can somebody help me with this issue? 
PS: Can I plot both estimated and predicted values on the map?

Thank you in advance.
Garry

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem: Prediction of the response on a grid/map.
parts:
Hi,
I couldn’t find a line where you define pred.ind, which is used to index the results.
The field given to inla.mesh.project needs to be a vector of length mesh$n, defining the field on each mesh node.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem: Prediction of the response on a grid/map.
parts:
The A matrix you use in stack.pred uses points commented as being point for unavailabledata, but if you want to index using only those point you won’t get the entire field. You could make the prediction stack predict at all mesh nodes, regardless of whether they have data or not. That would allow the inla.mesh.project/or code to work properly.
Alternatively, to save space, extract further indexing information from your current stack, relating to both est and pred, that together would give you all of the locations.

Finn
